- **Pivot:** `partition` always uses the last element, `arr[len - 1]`.
- **Recursion:** `quicksort` splits the slice at the pivot's final index. It recurses on the left part and on the right part after skipping the pivot.
- **Worst case:** O(n²) time. Because the pivot is always the last element, an already sorted, reverse-sorted or all-equal input gives the worst split. Each partition peels off one element, leaving a subproblem of size n−1, so the total work is about n²/2 comparisons.
- **Stack depth:** in that same worst case the recursion goes about n levels deep, so stack space is O(n). A large sorted input could overflow the stack.
- **Average and best case:** O(n log n).

The all-equal case is not mentioned in the file's doc comment, which only lists sorted and reverse-sorted input. It hits the worst case too, because `<=` sends every equal element to the left side.
